title: Test CCP2 queued expiry and generation invalidation
description:
Scope: one CCP2 queue/invalidation scenario module under /home/mark/Developer/lichen-workspace/project-LICHEN/python/tests/sim/scenarios/, reusing actual native-peer queue, CCA and driver-submission paths. Inject expiry or generation change between initial admission, deferral and submission; verify bounded back-pressure, priority and explicitly replaceable status updates. Expected queue/service/drop traces come from the independent corpus. Do not alter custody eviction/TTL policy, coalesce arbitrary messages, add an ACK or weaken existing queue tests.

HPC8 execution policy: Code, test, or schema changes require three independent correctness, security, and robustness reviews; file and fix all findings and re-review. Use independent oracles, never weakened legacy tests or self-generated expected results. Preserve upstream Yggdrasil addressing, radio-owned identity, best-effort custody, baseline SCHC, and the human-only OSCORE/EDHOC security edit bar. External actions, hardware/RF operations, and port access require scoped explicit permission and applicable bench safety checks. Research may conclude no-go; an authorization gate requires affirmative, recorded approval for its actual scope. Dependency closure and decomposition are not permission. No speculative activation, including deferred portability or experimental modes.
design: Keep this a focused integration family rather than a new queue implementation. Accounting and full-operation timing violations are additionally covered by the independent admission supplement.
acceptance_criteria: Expired or stale-generation frames cause no actual driver TX even if initially admitted. Queue capacity and existing back-pressure remain bounded; priorities order only eligible work. Status coalescing affects only explicitly replaceable data and preserves ordinary/historical messages. Deterministic observed enqueue/service/drop sequences match the independent oracle, including CCA deferral and invalidation immediately before submission. No denial is interpreted as SF12 selection or successful delivery.
